key_insight: For arrangements of at most 16 complex projective lines, the intersection lattice determines the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle.
engineering_relevance: For symbolic geometry software, this identifies when combinatorial intersection data suffice to determine bundle splitting and freeness without relying on explicit line coordinates.
method: Reduce to critical arrangements of 2s+3 lines with constrained intersection counts and minimal Jacobian syzygy degree s.
Bound the derivation’s zero scheme using inflection-polynomial factorization, Chern classes, Riccati equations, and Ziegler multirestriction.
Combine computer-algebra-verified local calculations with exhaustive candidate-lattice enumeration.
evidence_signal: The proof includes exhaustive enumeration of 26,265,318 candidate lattices satisfying Bojanowski’s inequality in the remaining zero-scheme-length cases 2 and 3.
watch_item: The general splitting-type result is limited to at most 16 lines; extensions to arbitrary sizes require the stated syzygy-degree or freeness hypotheses.
paper_title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
